originStory.title: Why Client Understanding Matters
originStory.subtitle: Lessons from watching brilliant code go to waste
originStory.story:
In my 30+ years of building software, I've seen too much brilliant code go to waste. Features that took weeks to build, never used. Perfect implementations of the wrong solution. I've been on both sides of that frustration.

The hard truth? Technical skills alone aren't enough. You can write beautiful code, but if it doesn't solve what clients actually need, you've wasted everyone's time. Including your own.

This book exists because I want you to stop building the wrong things. I want you to understand how to discover what users truly need, how to think about design, and how to create specifications that lead to success. These are the skills that separate developers who ship features from developers who ship value.
originStory.inspirationPoint: Stop building the wrong things. Start delivering real value.

creatorJourney.title: Lessons from Building Real Products
creatorJourney.subtitle: From painful failures to systematic success
creatorJourney.story: Early in my career, I learned the hard way that clients don't always know what they need. And neither did I. Projects failed not because of bad code, but because we built the wrong things. Everything changed when I discovered User-Centered Design and Jobs-To-Be-Done theory. Now I teach developers to ask the right questions before writing code.
struggles: Building features that clients never used
Discovering requirements too late in the project
Realizing technical excellence doesn't guarantee project success
achievements: Built products for clients across multiple industries
Learned requirements discovery through real project successes and failures
Applied UX principles to ship software users actually love
